title: Residency + Retention: SOC2/ISO Evidence Pipeline and Control Mapping
creator: Asha Menon
description: Goal: Define and deliver an automated evidence pipeline that maps Redwood Inference controls for data residency and retention to SOC 2 and ISO 27001 artifacts. The pipeline should collect, normalize, and store timestamped artifacts (logs, config snapshots, access lists, encryption key rotations, deletion records) tied to named controls so auditors can generate control reports on demand. This ticket covers control mapping, collector design, artifact retention policies, residency-aware storage placement, and reporting templates. Not scope: manual audit interviews and vendor attestations (these will be separate tasks).
acceptance_criteria: 1) A control matrix mapping Redwood-specific controls to SOC 2 (CC2, CC3, CC6 etc.) and ISO 27001 clauses with a canonical artifact type per control. 2) End-to-end collector proof-of-concept that captures three artifact types: access policy snapshot, KMS rotation event, and retention deletion log; artifacts are timestamped and stored in residency- and retention-aware buckets. 3) Console view (read-only) that can query artifacts by control id, date range, and region; exportable as PDF/CSV. 4) Automated daily digest report to Compliance mailing list with new artifacts and retention exceptions. 5) Security review and legal sign-off recorded in artifacts.
design_notes:
- Use a lightweight collector pattern: event-forwarder + transformer to canonical schema (artifact_type, control_ids, region, timestamp, origin_url, hash).
- Store artifacts in region-tagged object stores (S3 buckets or equivalent) with lifecycle rules aligned to retention settings per artifact/control.
- For residency constraints provide tag-based placement and an immutable index for audit tracing.
- Retention TTLs should be configurable per-project and per-customer when in Dedicated/Private modes; hosted API defaults enforced by policy.
- Map SOC 2 controls to observable artifacts: e.g., CC6 (Logical Access) -> IAM policy snapshots, P-2 (Encryption) -> KMS key rotation events, CC7 (Change Management) -> deployment manifests and PR links.
- ISO 27001 mapping aligned to Annex A controls; show clause references in matrix.
retention_policy_summary: Default hosted artifacts: 3 years for SOC-related artifacts, 7 years for legal-critical artifacts; Dedicated/Private: configurable between 1 day and 10 years via console with guardrails. Retention exceptions require legal ticket and are logged as artifacts.
data_residency_rules: Artifacts must be stored in a region matching the data residency configuration for the customer. For multi-region customers, primary residency region is authoritative; backups may be in DR region only when explicitly allowed and must be flagged. Console-level toggle controls residency enforcement; system will fail collectors if placement cannot be satisfied.
reporting_and_export:
- On-demand control report that bundles all artifacts tagged to a control into a zip with manifest.json.
- Scheduled weekly evidence digests for compliance team.
- Export formats: PDF summary, CSV manifest, TAR of raw artifacts.
- Audit trail: each export gets its own artifact entry with who/when and hash.
open_questions: 1) For Dedicated customers, do we allow cross-region backups by default or require opt-in? (Security asked for opt-in)
2) Do we store full raw artifacts or only hashes + pointers for privacy-sensitive items? (Legal prefers pointers for PII-heavy artifacts)
3) How granular must control mapping be for ISO auditors vs SOC auditors? (PM recommendation: offer two levels: summary and full-detail exports)
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: retention misconfiguration could violate customer agreements -> Mitigation: add automated policy validator and preflight check in Console before applying retention changes.
Risk: collectors accidentally send PII to non-resident regions -> Mitigation: residency enforcement at collector with fail-open disabled and auditor traces.
Risk: storage costs escalate with long retention -> Mitigation: tiered lifecycle; compress and store hashes for low-value artifacts.
Risk: auditors need ad-hoc artifacts beyond mapped types -> Mitigation: run ad-hoc collector on demand and capture a signed export artifact.
